5. Repeat with `fixtures/ellis-1818.jpg` and tap **None of these**. You should get the epitaph with "No public record was confirmed" and no AI label.

## Expect
- Slow steps are likely on the free tier. If research or story takes more than about 30 s, note which step.
- Chambers (2011) may end on the epitaph if the records only repeat his dates. Tell me what you see.

I'll run Lighthouse against `pnpm preview` once you report back. Tell me the timing and anything odd, and I'll mark T040 and stop the server.
The server is fine: it answers on 172.20.1.18 from this Mac. The problem is the network. This Mac isn't on Wi-Fi (it's on a wired or other interface at 172.20.x.x), so a phone on Wi-Fi is probably on a different subnet, or the network blocks device-to-device traffic.

## Fixes, easiest first
1. **Put the Mac on the phone's Wi-Fi.** Join the same network, then tell me. The IP will change, so I'll restart the server and give you the new URL.
2. **Use the phone's hotspot.** Connect the Mac to it. Hotspots don't isolate clients, and I'll give you the new URL.
3. **Test from the phone's browser first.** Open `http://172.20.1.18:5199/`. If it times out on office or guest Wi-Fi, the network is isolating clients, so use option 1 or 2.

## Avoid
A public tunnel (ngrok or cloudflared). The dev server carries your live Gemini and SerpApi keys, so anyone with the link could spend your quota. I won't set one up unless you ask.

Tell me which option you pick.
Nothing has changed on this Mac: it still has the same address (172.20.1.18), and the server is still up and answering locally. The same URL is the one to try on the phone.

If you switched networks, this Mac didn't pick it up. Tell me which option you used (same Wi-Fi, hotspot, or just retrying the URL) and what the phone shows: a timeout, "can't connect", or a blank page. A timeout means the network is isolating devices, so the next step would be the phone's hotspot.
